newsitem.title: ANGOLA: ANGOLA DEPORTS S.AFRICA DIAMOND MINERS--AMBASSADOR.
newsitem.headline: ANGOLA DEPORTS S.AFRICA DIAMOND MINERS--AMBASSADOR.

text.p: The Angolan government deported 18 South African miners on Wednesday, accusing them of working in the country's diamond areas without legal work permits, said South Africa's ambassador in the government-controlled capital.
"I can confirm that the South African Airways plane left at 1.15 p.m. today (1215 GMT) carrying all 18 of them," Ambassador Roger Ballard-Tremer told Reuters.
"The government said the deportation did not signal that they could not return. They would be welcome to return to Angola but with proper documents," he added.
The 18 men had been held at a Luanda prison for over a week.

Angola launched a national campaign to root out foreigners operating illegally in the country and toughened immigration laws last month. Until now the Cancer II operation has netted more than 1,000 foreigners, mostly from West Africa.

Three of the South Africans were arrested in Saurimo, the capital of Lunda Sul province, after being accused of entering the country on an illegal flight from Cape Town and failing to clear their equipment through customs.
The other 15 men were arrested at N'Giva in Cunene province, for allegedly failing to pay import duties on equipment and entering the country on visitor permits instead of work visas.
Both groups had been contracted to work on diamond concessions in Lunda Norte province where most of Angola's diamonds are found.

Representatives of several South African mining companies who were meeting in Luanda at the weekend told Reuters they were in the country seeking help from South African and Angolan authorities to get back equipment worth millions of dollars.

They accused generals and businessmen who own concessions in Lunda Norte of cheating their South African partners by having them pay for equipment which was then "hijacked" once it arrived at the site.
